summary: Joel pictures this locust eating what an earlier swarm has left. Jeremiah likens invading troops and horses to it, while Nahum draws on both its numbers and its sudden departure.

senses.definition: A locust that strips crops and can appear in countless numbers.

evidence.note: The yeleq eats what the ʾarbeh leaves, then the ḥāsīl takes what the yeleq leaves.
Yahweh promises to make good the years of harvest eaten by these pests.
In the account of Egypt’s plagues, the locusts arrive in numbers beyond counting.
The attackers who will fill Babylon are compared to a swarm.
The horses mustered against Babylon resemble bristling locusts.
The comparison appears twice, first in connection with devouring, then in the taunt to multiply.
The sudden departure of a locust that flies away follows the description of Nineveh’s numerous merchants.

note: The noun’s origin remains uncertain. The proposed link to licking draws on the insect’s appetite. The flight in Nahum 3:16 makes an exclusively wingless interpretation doubtful. Jemuel and Jemimah, indexed nearby, have no demonstrated connection to the locust.
